source_basis.predecessor_source_reuse: This run is a computational continuation of the source-backed exact-curtailment/tail-floor model in the predecessor checkpoint; no new public-source claim is introduced.

problem.terminal_action: commit iff W_r >= k among r discordant signs, realized with exact deterministic curtailment
problem.objective: maximize worst-position probability of committing the single q=.60 true improvement subject to all-null FWER<=.05 and a 95th-percentile total paired-observation budget

method.statistical_evaluation: Exact binomial null/alternative tail probabilities; exact all-null false-commit survival; exact within-candidate curtailed stopping distribution; total discordance distribution convolved along the survival path; fixed-rho pair-count CDF obtained as the exact mixture of negative-binomial waiting-time CDFs.
method.fixed_depth_benchmark: Previously derived fixed-r deterministic maximin survival-path policies plus exact q95 re-evaluation after curtailment.
method.mixed_depth_search: Generated deterministic target-power policies with residual-alpha/tail-floor state, mean-discordance Pareto pruning, and exact q95 readout; then applied direct budget-constrained local neighbor search over (r,k) action sequences and exact q95 feasibility at each sampled budget.
method.certification: All reported operating characteristics for the listed policies are exact under the stated model. The mixed-depth policy search is not a proof of global q95-optimality because the proposal stage uses Pareto pruning/local search; values are a reproducible lower bound on the achievable mixed-depth frontier, not a certified upper envelope.

key_results.result: Mixed depth is nearly irrelevant at very low budgets and at the fully deep endpoint, but creates a large mid-budget power bridge. At q95 budget 2000, an observed r30:k23 x18 then r50:k36 x2 policy has exact q95=1941, worst-position q=.60 true-commit=0.0416317, FWER=0.0484578, versus the best fixed-depth policy available below the same budget at 0.0171830 worst-position power (about +142% relative).

The strongest observed relative gains occur before the fixed-r50 family becomes affordable: at budgets 2750 and 3000, observed mixed-depth worst-position power is 0.0497583 and 0.0509520 versus fixed-depth 0.0171830, roughly +190% and +197% relative.

At q95 budget 3250, an observed mixed schedule reaches worst-position power 0.0531186 with q95=3192, while the best fixed-depth policy below 3250 reaches 0.0279491 at q95=3228; the mixed schedule uses r50:k36 x13, r50:k35 x5, then r30:k22 x2.

At q95 budget 1000, exact curtailment already makes the fixed-r20 maximin policy feasible (q95=992, power=0.0156757); mixed-depth search did not improve its worst-position power. At budget 3500, the fixed-r50 maximin endpoint (q95=3389, power=0.0534655) also remains the best observed endpoint.

rejected_or_narrowed_generalizations: Rejected: after exact curtailment, a single fixed discordant depth is sufficient across all cost budgets. In the tested q=.60, rho=.20, 20-candidate model, mixed depths can more than double worst-position power across a broad mid-budget region.

Narrowed: mixed depth is always beneficial. The observed gain is negligible below about 1000 pairs, zero at the 1000-pair fixed-r20 point, and zero again once the fixed-r50 maximin endpoint is affordable around 3389 pairs.

Narrowed: the listed mixed policies are the exact global Pareto frontier. Their operating characteristics are exact, but global search optimality is not yet certified because candidate generation used mean-cost Pareto pruning and local search.

frontier.action: Certify or tighten the q95 Pareto envelope with a distribution-aware dynamic program/branch-and-bound that prunes on exact all-null cost distributions rather than mean discordance; focus first on the 1800-3300 pair region where mixed depth showed the largest gains.

Generalize the cost constraint from fixed rho=.20 to candidate/history-varying discordance rates while preserving sign symmetry; derive conservative q95 bounds or robust policies over rho in [.20,.60].

After the deterministic mixed-depth envelope is certified, test stochastic shallow-to-deep/deepening rules that alter the terminal event and quantify any additional cost savings against exact power/FWER changes.
Add wall-clock/batched execution cost because pair-count q95 may overstate elapsed-time savings when rollouts are parallelized.

exact_next_action: Build an exact distribution-aware branch-and-bound/DP over 20 survival-path actions using stopped-cost and surviving-prefix distributions, certify the best attainable worst-position q=.60 power at q95 budgets 1800, 2000, 2500, 3000 and 3250 under rho=.20, then extend the certified winners to rho uncertainty.
